title: Ryan Garcia retains WBC welterweight title, stops Conor Benn at 1:25 of second round
dek: Ryan Garcia retained his WBC welterweight title by stopping Conor Benn at 1 minute 25 seconds of the second round at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on September 12, 2026. The fight ended after Garcia landed a right hand that sent Benn to the canvas, and Benn was unable to continue after the referee stopped the bout.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Ryan Garcia retained his WBC welterweight title by stopping Conor Benn at 1:25 of the second round, with Benn, the WBC's number one contender, unable to mount a credible offense before being knocked down and the fight being halted.
bottom_line: García's focus now turns to Teófimo López, whom he called out at ringside. The welterweight title picture sits in flux between García, López, and Devin Haney, the WBO champion. Benn's path back from a 96-second knockout at world-title level remains undefined; the decision rests with him and Zuffa.
body:
Ryan Garcia retained his WBC welterweight title by stopping Conor Benn at 1 minute 25 seconds of the second round at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on September 12, 2026, per the Guardian. Garcia, 28 and American, improved to 26-2 with 21 KOs. Benn, 29 and from Essex, Britain, fell to 25-2 with 14 KOs.
Benn entered as the WBC's number one contender and BoxRec's highest-ranked British welterweight, according to BBC Sport. Yet the contender's path to a world title shot bypassed the traditional route. BBC Sport reports that Benn turned professional with limited amateur experience, bypassed the traditional British, Commonwealth and European title path, and built much of his reputation fighting against ageing former champions.
The fight exposed that gap. In the opening round, Benn aggressively came forward while Garcia picked him off on the counter, per BBC Sport. Garcia landed two sharp left hooks early on. Although Benn initially appeared to take the shots well, Garcia soon found gaps as the Briton charged into range, according to BBC Sport. Benn's plan to pressure Garcia from the opening bell and deliver "tenacity, ferocity, spite" throughout the build-up never materialized into sustained offense.
In the second round, a left uppercut from Garcia staggered Benn, per BBC Sport.  Benn beat the count but was a sitting target as Garcia attacked again, forcing the referee to step in as the challenger was pinned against the ropes, according to BBC Sport. BBC Sport notes there were some suggestions ringside that the stoppage came early, with Benn still moving and trying to evade shots, but the referee was justified in preventing further punishment.
Garcia disputed any suggestion the stoppage was premature. He told the Guardian: "They could have stopped it when he was on the ground. He was out of it. I looked at him in the eyes and he wasn't even there. If it would've kept going, you would've seen a man unconscious on the floor. It's the ref's job to stop the fight when it needs to be done, to protect the fighter."
The fight unfolded under unusual circumstances. Benn had not fought at the welterweight limit of 147 pounds in more than four years, having campaigned as high as middleweight. He described the process of returning to 147 pounds as going through the "pits of hell." Benn came in at 146 pounds at Friday's weigh-in, his lightest in seven years, per the Guardian. Without a rehydration clause, Benn looked strikingly bigger in the ring and posted footage on Friday evening suggesting he was 32 pounds heavier than at the official weigh-in, although BBC Sport notes that figure was not independently verified.
After the fight, Benn was taken to hospital, understood to be a precautionary measure, per BBC Sport. Benn did not attend the post-fight news conference, per BBC Sport. The decision about his future remains uncertain. Zuffa Boxing chief Dana White largely sidestepped questions about Benn's next move, per BBC Sport: "Let Conor go home, spend some time with his family, enjoy the success he had this year. When he's ready to come back and lets us know, we'll figure out what's next for him."
Benn has not ruled out a trilogy fight with Chris Eubank Jr., and he had said before the fight that he planned to move up in weight regardless of Saturday's result, per BBC Sport. When asked whether moving up against bigger opponents could prove even more dangerous, White said: "We'll see. We'll see how the whole thing figures out."
The ringside atmosphere shaped the narrative. A crowd of 18,855 at T-Mobile Arena, mostly pro-Garcia, watched as Teófimo López taunted Garcia from ringside and threatened to storm the ring, per the Guardian. After the stoppage, Garcia spotted López and summoned him, shouting: "Unified time. Where you at, Teo?" When López responded, Garcia escalated, per the Guardian: "You want to get crazy, we going to get crazy. I'll beat your ass right now." García also made a challenge to Devin Haney, the WBO champion who was an interested observer at ringside, per the Guardian.
Garcia won the welterweight title by flooring and outpointing Mario Barrios at the same arena in February, per the Guardian. Both fighters in Saturday's bout were reportedly earning around 15 million dollars apiece, per the Guardian. The fight was co-promoted by Zuffa Boxing and Oscar De La Hoya's Golden Boy. Zuffa Boxing poached Benn in April after his entire 10-year career with Eddie Hearn's Matchroom, per the Guardian. When asked whether Benn had still been worth the money to Zuffa (reportedly 11 million pounds to sign), White bluntly said: "Every penny of it," per BBC Sport.
Garcia's superior amateur pedigree, greater experience at the highest level and natural talent were simply too much for Benn, as many predicted, per BBC Sport. The manner of defeat will inevitably strengthen the argument that Benn was not ready for a world-title shot, per BBC Sport. However, BBC Sport notes that Benn remains one of British boxing's most recognisable fighters and, as a prominent signing to Zuffa Boxing, there will still be opportunities.
Garcia, in his post-fight interview with DAZN, reflected on the fight's arc: "The first round I was just saying, 'Just protect yourself. He's going to get crazy. Just really worry about just watching what he's doing, download, download, download.' Then I started hitting him. I was like, 'Oh wow, I'm already timing him.' And then the second round I said, 'I'm just going to stand my ground a little bit. I'm going to get my respect real quick. And then when I did, I ended up knocking him out." He added: "We got to clear this [division] out."
